subproblems.title: H^n restricted to a countably n-rectifiable set is σ-finite
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ and let M ⊆ ℝ^N be countably n-rectifiable in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.1 (Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n M). That is, M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_{j∈ℕ} F_j(ℝ^n) with H^n(M₀) = 0 and each F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^N Lipschitz. Then the measure H^n⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M on ℝ^N is σ-finite.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclidean N)), Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n M → SigmaFinite ((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)).restrict M)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: H := μHE[n] on ℝ^N = Euclidean N. On ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) we also use μHE[n]. Put ν := H.restrict M.

1. Unfold the hypothesis (Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable). There are M₀ ⊆ ℝ^N with H(M₀) = 0 and maps F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^N (j ∈ ℕ), each K_j-Lipschitz for some K_j ∈ ℝ≥0 (choose K_j for every j), with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j.

2. For j, k ∈ ℕ put C_{j,k} := F_j '' closedBall(0, k) ⊆ ℝ^N. The closed ball is compact (ℝ^n is proper) and F_j is continuous, being Lipschitz. So C_{j,k} is compact, hence closed and measurable.

3. H(C_{j,k}) < ∞. By definition (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def), μHE[n] = c • μH[n] on every metric space, with the same scalar c := addHaarScalarFactor(volume on ℝ^n, μH[n]) ∈ ℝ≥0, which depends only on n. The Lipschitz bound LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le (dimension (n:ℝ) ≥ 0) gives μH[n](F_j '' s) ≤ K_j^n · μH[n](s) for every s ⊆ ℝ^n. Multiplying by c and regrouping gives H(C_{j,k}) ≤ K_j^n · μHE[n](closedBall(0,k)), where the last measure is taken in ℝ^n. In ℝ^n, μHE[n] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), and volume(closedBall(0,k)) < ∞ (measure_closedBall_lt_top). Since (K_j : ℝ≥0∞)^n < ∞, H(C_{j,k}) < ∞.

4. Let S := toMeasurable H M₀ ∪ ⋃_{(j,k)∈ℕ×ℕ} C_{j,k}. S is measurable. We show M ⊆ S. Let x ∈ M. Either x ∈ M₀ ⊆ toMeasurable H M₀ (subset_toMeasurable), or x = F_j(y) for some j and some y ∈ ℝ^n. In the second case choose k ∈ ℕ with ‖y‖ ≤ k (exists_nat_ge). Then y ∈ closedBall(0,k), so x ∈ C_{j,k}.

5. Consider the countable family 𝒮 := {Sᶜ, toMeasurable H M₀} ∪ {C_{j,k} : (j,k) ∈ ℕ×ℕ}. Its union is ℝ^N: a point of S lies in toMeasurable H M₀ or in some C_{j,k}, and any other point lies in Sᶜ.

6. Every member of 𝒮 has finite ν-measure. All members are measurable, so ν(A) = H(A ∩ M) for each of them (Measure.restrict_apply).
 (a) ν(Sᶜ) = H(Sᶜ ∩ M) = H(∅) = 0, because M ⊆ S by step 4.
 (b) ν(toMeasurable H M₀) ≤ H(toMeasurable H M₀) = H(M₀) = 0 (measure_toMeasurable).
 (c) ν(C_{j,k}) ≤ H(C_{j,k}) < ∞ by step 3.

7. A measure is σ-finite when a countable family of sets of finite measure covers the whole space (Measure.sigmaFinite_of_countable). By steps 5–6, ν = μHE[n].restrict M is σ-finite. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unfold CountablyRectifiable: M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j with H^n(M₀) = 0 and F_j K_j-Lipschitz.
H^n(F_j(closedBall 0 k)) ≤ K_j^n·vol_n(closedBall 0 k) < ∞, from LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, μHE[n] = c•μH[n], and μHE[n] = volume on ℝ^n.
S := toMeasurable H M₀ ∪ ⋃_{j,k} F_j(closedBall 0 k) contains M; the countable family {Sᶜ, toMeasurable H M₀, F_j(closedBall 0 k)} covers ℝ^N.
Each member has finite (H⌞M)-measure (0, 0, or ≤ H^n(F_j(B_k)) < ∞), so Measure.sigmaFinite_of_countable gives σ-finiteness.

subproblems.title: μ-null sets of positive n-density are H^n-null (Simon Ch. 1, 3.3 with outer regularity)
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ and let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N. Let θ : ℝ^N → ℝ, and let Z ⊆ ℝ^N with μ(Z) = 0 (outer measure). Suppose every x ∈ Z has θ(x) > 0 and Θ^n(μ, x) = θ(x), i.e. μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) → θ(x) as ρ ↓ 0 with closed balls (HasDensity n μ x (ofReal θ(x))). Then H^n(Z) = 0, where H^n = μHE[n].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (Z : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ), (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → μ K ≠ ∞) → μ Z = 0 → (∀ x ∈ Z, 0 < θ x ∧ HasDensity n μ x (ENNReal.ofReal (θ x))) → μHE[n] Z = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Imports needed in Submission: Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.DensityComparison (simon_theorem_3_3), Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.EuclideanHausdorffUpper (volume_euclidean_ball_eq), Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLiteral (simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure). Write H := μHE[n] on ℝ^N.

1. The unit-ball constants agree: Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume (n:ℝ) = unitBallVolume n, where unitBallVolume n is the volume of the open unit ball of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n).
 - If n ≥ 1: Chapter01.volume_euclidean_ball_eq (with 0 < n) at centre 0 and radius 1 gives volume(ball 0 1) = realUnitBallVolume n · ofReal(1)^n = realUnitBallVolume n.
 - If n = 0: realUnitBallVolume 0 = 1 (Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume_zero). EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 0) is a single point, so ball 0 1 = univ. The map PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp (Fin 0) is volume preserving, so volume(univ) equals the volume of univ in Fin 0 → ℝ. That volume is Measure.pi over the empty index set (MeasureTheory.volume_pi), and Measure.pi_univ gives the empty product 1.

2. Regularity. Since μ(K) < ∞ for all compact K, μ is finite on compacts. Hence it is locally finite on the locally compact space ℝ^N, and therefore regular (ℝ^N is σ-compact and metrizable); in particular it is outer regular. So for every set A ⊆ ℝ^N and every r > μ(A) there is an open O ⊇ A with μ(O) < r (Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt, valid for arbitrary A).

3. Normalisation. For every A ⊆ ℝ^N, Chapter01.simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal (n:ℝ) A = H(A). Indeed, simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal (n:ℝ) = (simonHausdorffMeasureReal (n:ℝ)).toOuterMeasure by Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure (as 0 ≤ n), and simonHausdorffMeasureReal (n:ℝ) = μHE[n] by Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure.

4. Reduction. For k ∈ ℕ let t_k := 1/(k+1) > 0 and Z_k := {x ∈ Z : t_k ≤ θ(x)}. (Index by k+1, since 1/0 = 0.) If x ∈ Z then θ(x) > 0, so some k has 1/(k+1) < θ(x) (exists_nat_one_div_lt). Hence Z ⊆ ⋃_k Z_k. By countable subadditivity (measure_iUnion_null, measure_mono_null) it suffices to show H(Z_k) = 0 for each k. Fix k and write t := t_k. Then μ(Z_k) ≤ μ(Z) = 0.

5. Fix ε > 0 in ℝ≥0∞. By step 2 with A = Z_k (μ(Z_k) = 0 < ε) there is an open O ⊇ Z_k with μ(O) < ε.

6. Density at points of Z_k relative to O. Let y ∈ Z_k. Since O is open and y ∈ O, there is δ > 0 with ball(y,δ) ⊆ O (Metric.isOpen_iff). For 0 < r < δ we have closedBall(y,r) ⊆ ball(y,δ) ⊆ O, so μ(O ∩ closedBall(y,r)) = μ(closedBall(y,r)). Hence SimonGMT's quotient Chapter01.dimensionalDensityQuotient μ.toOuterMeasure (n:ℝ) O y r = μ(O ∩ closedBall(y,r)) / (realUnitBallVolume (n:ℝ) · ofReal(r)^(n:ℝ)) equals densityRatio n μ y r = μ(closedBall(y,r)) / (unitBallVolume n · ofReal(r)^n). This uses step 1 and ofReal(r)^(n:ℝ) = ofReal(r)^n (ENNReal.rpow_natCast). Since (0,δ) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT), the two functions are eventually equal along 𝓝[>] 0, so their limsups agree (Filter.limsup_congr). By hypothesis densityRatio n μ y → ofReal θ(y) along 𝓝[>] 0 (HasDensity), so its limsup is ofReal θ(y) (Tendsto.limsup_eq). Therefore Chapter01.dimensionalUpperDensity μ.toOuterMeasure (n:ℝ) O y = ofReal θ(y) ≥ ofReal t, because t ≤ θ(y).

7. Apply Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.3 (Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_3) to the outer measure μ.toOuterMeasure. It is Borel regular by Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular. Take dimension (n:ℝ) ≥ 0, A₁ := Z_k ⊆ A₂ := O and threshold t ≥ 0. Step 6 is exactly its hypothesis ofReal t ≤ dimensionalUpperDensity μ.toOuterMeasure n O y for all y ∈ Z_k. The theorem yields ofReal t · simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal (n:ℝ) Z_k ≤ μ.toOuterMeasure O = μ(O). By steps 3 and 5, ofReal t · H(Z_k) ≤ μ(O) < ε.

8. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, ofReal t · H(Z_k) = 0 (e.g. by ENNReal.le_of_forall_pos_le_add). As t > 0, ofReal t ≠ 0, so H(Z_k) = 0. By step 4, H(Z) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: ω_n agreement: realUnitBallVolume (n:ℝ) = unitBallVolume n (volume_euclidean_ball_eq for n ≥ 1; n = 0 directly via PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp and Measure.pi over an empty index).

μ is finite on compacts, hence outer regular; H^n is SimonGMT's simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n via simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure and simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure.
Split Z = ⋃_k Z_k with Z_k = {x ∈ Z : θ(x) ≥ 1/(k+1)}; μ(Z_k) = 0; choose open O ⊇ Z_k with μ(O) < ε.
For y ∈ Z_k, small closed balls lie in O, so dimensionalUpperDensity μ n O y = lim densityRatio = ofReal θ(y) ≥ ofReal(1/(k+1)).
simon_theorem_3_3 gives ofReal(1/(k+1))·H^n(Z_k) ≤ μ(O) < ε for all ε, so H^n(Z_k) = 0 and H^n(Z) = 0.

subproblems.title: From the approximate-tangent set to all of M: μ = θ H^n⌞M on Borel sets (B3a)
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, H := μHE[n] on ℝ^N, and let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K. Let M ⊆ ℝ^N be such that H⌞M is s-finite, and let E ⊆ M. Let θ : ℝ^N → ℝ satisfy θ(x) > 0 and HasDensity n μ x (ofReal θ(x)) for every x ∈ M. If μ(B) = ∫⁻_{E∩B} ofReal(θ) dH for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^N, then μ(B) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} ofReal(θ) dH for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^N.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (M E : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ), (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → μ K ≠ ∞) → SFinite ((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)).restrict M) → E ⊆ M → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x ∧ HasDensity n μ x (ENNReal.ofReal (θ x))) → (∀ B : Set (Euclidean N), MeasurableSet B → μ B = ∫⁻ x in E ∩ B, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ∂μHE[n]) → ∀ B : Set (Euclidean N), MeasurableSet B → μ B = ∫⁻ x in M ∩ B, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: H := μHE[n]; ν := H.restrict M, which is s-finite by hypothesis; f(x) := ofReal(θ(x)).

1. Measurable hull of E for ν. Let B* := toMeasurable ν E. Then B* is measurable and E ⊆ B* (subset_toMeasurable). Since ν is s-finite, ν(B* ∩ D) = ν(E ∩ D) for every measurable D (Measure.measure_toMeasurable_inter_of_sFinite).

2. μ(M ∖ B*) = 0. Apply the hypothesis to the Borel set B*ᶜ: μ(B*ᶜ) = ∫⁻_{E ∩ B*ᶜ} f dH. Since E ⊆ B*, E ∩ B*ᶜ = ∅. The restriction of H to ∅ is the zero measure, so the integral is 0 and μ(B*ᶜ) = 0. As M ∖ B* ⊆ B*ᶜ, μ(M ∖ B*) = 0.

3. H(M ∖ B*) = 0. Apply the sibling child hausdorff_null_of_weight_null (Submission.allard_tc_tpr_hausdorff_null_of_weight_null) to this μ, Z := M ∖ B* and θ. Its hypotheses hold: μ is finite on compact sets; μ(Z) = 0 by step 2; and every x ∈ Z lies in M, so θ(x) > 0 and HasDensity n μ x (ofReal θ(x)).

4. Fix a Borel set B. Claim: H.restrict(E ∩ B) = H.restrict(M ∩ B). By Measure.ext it suffices to compare the two measures on a measurable set D. By Measure.restrict_apply, we must show H(D ∩ (E ∩ B)) = H(D ∩ (M ∩ B)).
 (≤) D ∩ (E ∩ B) ⊆ D ∩ (M ∩ B) because E ⊆ M; use monotonicity.
 (≥) Each x ∈ D ∩ (M ∩ B) lies in (B* ∩ (D ∩ B)) ∩ M if x ∈ B*, and in M ∖ B* otherwise. By subadditivity and step 3,
 H(D ∩ (M ∩ B)) ≤ H((B* ∩ (D ∩ B)) ∩ M) + H(M ∖ B*) = H((B* ∩ (D ∩ B)) ∩ M).
 The set B* ∩ (D ∩ B) is measurable, so H((B* ∩ (D ∩ B)) ∩ M) = ν(B* ∩ (D ∩ B)) (Measure.restrict_apply). By step 1 (D ∩ B is measurable) this equals ν(E ∩ (D ∩ B)). Since E ∩ (D ∩ B) ⊆ M, ν(E ∩ (D ∩ B)) = H(E ∩ (D ∩ B)) (Measure.restrict_eq_self; no measurability of E or M is needed). Finally E ∩ (D ∩ B) = D ∩ (E ∩ B), which proves (≥).

5. The set integrals ∫⁻_{E∩B} f dH and ∫⁻_{M∩B} f dH are lintegrals against the two measures of step 4, so they are equal. By hypothesis μ(B) = ∫⁻_{E∩B} f dH, hence μ(B) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} f dH. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take the measurable hull B* := toMeasurable (H⌞M) E; s-finiteness gives (H⌞M)(B* ∩ D) = (H⌞M)(E ∩ D) for measurable D.
μ(B*ᶜ) = ∫⁻ over E ∩ B*ᶜ = ∅, so it is 0; hence μ(M ∖ B*) = 0.
Sibling hausdorff_null_of_weight_null with positive density on M gives H^n(M ∖ B*) = 0.
For Borel B and measurable D: H(D∩M∩B) ≤ H(B*∩D∩B∩M) + H(M∖B*) = (H⌞M)(B*∩D∩B) = (H⌞M)(E∩D∩B) = H(D∩E∩B); so H⌞(E∩B) = H⌞(M∩B).
Therefore μ(B) = ∫⁻_{E∩B} θ dH^n = ∫⁻_{M∩B} θ dH^n.

subproblems.title: Integration against μ = θ H^n⌞M
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, H := μHE[n] on ℝ^N, and let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N. Let M ⊆ ℝ^N be H-null-measurable, and let θ : ℝ^N → ℝ with θ > 0 on M and θ H-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N. Suppose μ(B) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} ofReal(θ) dH for every Borel B. Then for every function g : ℝ^N → ℝ, ∫ g dμ = ∫_M g·θ dH (Bochner integrals, with Lean's convention for non-integrable functions).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ), NullMeasurableSet M μHE[n] → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) → (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) μHE[n]) → (∀ B : Set (Euclidean N), MeasurableSet B → μ B = ∫⁻ x in M ∩ B, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ∂μHE[n]) → ∀ g : Euclidean N → ℝ, ∫ z, g z ∂μ = ∫ z in M, g z * θ z ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: H := μHE[n]; ν := H.restrict M; f(x) := ofReal(θ(x)) ∈ [0,∞).

1. θ is ν-a.e. measurable. Every x ∈ ℝ^N lies in closedBall(0,k) for some k ∈ ℕ (exists_nat_ge applied to ‖x‖). Hence M = ⋃_{k∈ℕ} (M ∩ closedBall(0,k)). Each closedBall(0,k) is compact, so by hypothesis θ is H-integrable on M ∩ closedBall(0,k). In particular θ is a.e.-strongly measurable, hence a.e.-measurable, for H.restrict(M ∩ closedBall(0,k)). By aemeasurable_iUnion_iff (a countable union), θ is AEMeasurable for H.restrict(⋃_k M ∩ closedBall(0,k)) = ν. Therefore f = ofReal ∘ θ is AEMeasurable for ν (AEMeasurable.ennreal_ofReal).

2. μ = ν.withDensity f. Let B be measurable. Then (ν.withDensity f)(B) = ∫⁻_B f dν (withDensity_apply) = ∫⁻ f d(H.restrict(B ∩ M)) (Measure.restrict_restrict, B measurable) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} f dH (B ∩ M = M ∩ B) = μ(B) by hypothesis. Measures that agree on all measurable sets are equal (Measure.ext).

3. f is ν-a.e. measurable (step 1) and f(x) < ∞ for every x. So integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ gives, for the given g : ℝ^N → ℝ,
 ∫ g dμ = ∫ g d(ν.withDensity f) = ∫ (f(x)).toReal · g(x) dν(x).
 This identity holds for arbitrary g; no measurability or integrability of g is needed.

4. For x ∈ M we have θ(x) > 0, so (ofReal θ(x)).toReal = θ(x) (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal). Since M is H-null-measurable, ν-a.e. x lies in M (ae_restrict_mem₀). Hence (f x).toReal · g(x) = g(x)·θ(x) for ν-a.e. x. By integral_congr_ae, ∫ (f x).toReal · g(x) dν = ∫_M g·θ dH. Together with step 3 this proves ∫ g dμ = ∫_M g·θ dH. ∎
proof_key_steps: θ is AEMeasurable for H⌞M, since M = ⋃_k M ∩ closedBall(0,k) and θ is integrable on each piece (aemeasurable_iUnion_iff).
μ = (H⌞M).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ), because both agree on measurable sets (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict).
integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ gives ∫ g dμ = ∫ (ofReal θ).toReal · g d(H⌞M) for every g.
On M, (ofReal θ).toReal = θ since θ > 0, and H⌞M-a.e. points lie in M (ae_restrict_mem₀); so ∫ g dμ = ∫_M gθ dH^n.

subproblems.title: Change of variables for H^n under the blow-up map η_{x,r}
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, H := μHE[n] on ℝ^N, M ⊆ ℝ^N any set, φ : ℝ^N → ℝ any function, x ∈ ℝ^N and r > 0. Let η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(z − x) (Chapter03.blowUpMap x r). Then ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} φ dH = r^{-n} ∫_M φ∘η_{x,r} dH (Bochner set integrals).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (φ : Euclidean N → ℝ) (x : Euclidean N) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → ∫ y in Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M, φ y ∂μHE[n] = r⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ z in M, φ (Chapter03.blowUpMap x r z) ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: H := μHE[n] on ℝ^N; η := Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, so η(z) = r⁻¹•(z − x); c := r⁻¹^n ≥ 0.

1. η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^N. It is the composite of the translation z ↦ z − x (Homeomorph.subRight x) and the dilation w ↦ r⁻¹•w (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero, since r⁻¹ ≠ 0). This composite agrees with η pointwise by definition of blowUpMap. Hence η is a measurable equivalence (Homeomorph.toMeasurableEquiv) and in particular a measurable embedding (MeasurableEquiv.measurableEmbedding).

2. Scaling holds for arbitrary sets. Let A ⊆ ℝ^N. Then η '' A = r⁻¹ • ((· − x) '' A) (Set.image_image, Set.image_smul). The translation z ↦ z − x is an isometry ((IsometryEquiv.subRight x).isometry), so H((· − x) '' A) = H(A) (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). For the nonzero scalar r⁻¹, H(r⁻¹ • A') = ‖r⁻¹‖₊^n • H(A') for every set A' (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀; this holds for non-measurable sets too). Since r > 0, ‖r⁻¹‖₊^n coerced to ℝ≥0∞ equals ofReal(r⁻¹^n). Hence H(η '' A) = ofReal(c) · H(A).

3. Measure identity: H.restrict(η '' M) = ofReal(c) • (H.restrict M).map η. Check this on a measurable set D (Measure.ext).
 - Left side: H(D ∩ η''M). For any map, η''(M ∩ η⁻¹'D) = η''M ∩ D (Set.image_inter_preimage). So the left side is H(η''(η⁻¹'D ∩ M)) = ofReal(c) · H(η⁻¹'D ∩ M) by step 2.
 - Right side: by Measure.smul_apply and Measure.map_apply (η measurable, D measurable) it is ofReal(c) · (H.restrict M)(η⁻¹'D). Since η⁻¹'D is measurable, Measure.restrict_apply turns this into ofReal(c) · H(η⁻¹'D ∩ M).
 The two sides agree.

4. Conclusion. By step 3, ∫_{η''M} φ dH = ∫ φ d(ofReal(c) • (H.restrict M).map η). By integral_smul_measure this equals (ofReal c).toReal · ∫ φ d((H.restrict M).map η). By MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map (valid for arbitrary φ, with no measurability assumption) and ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (c ≥ 0), this equals c · ∫ φ∘η d(H.restrict M) = r⁻¹^n · ∫_M φ(η z) dH(z). ∎
proof_key_steps: η_{x,r} = (dilation by r⁻¹) ∘ (translation by −x) is a homeomorphism, hence a measurable embedding.
For every set A: H^n(η''A) = r^{-n}·H^n(A), by Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀.
H⌞(η''M) = ofReal(r^{-n}) • (H⌞M).map η, checked on measurable D using Set.image_inter_preimage.
integral_smul_measure and MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map (arbitrary integrand) give ∫_{η''M} φ dH = r^{-n} ∫_M φ∘η dH.

subproblems.title: If μ_V = θ H^n⌞M, the varifold tangent plane at x is the unique approximate tangent plane of (M, θ) at x
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N, V an n-varifold on U, and H := μHE[n]. Let M ⊆ ℝ^N be H-null-measurable, and let θ : ℝ^N → ℝ with θ > 0 on M and θ H-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N. Suppose μ_V(B) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} ofReal(θ) dH for every Borel B. Let x ∈ ℝ^N and T ∈ G(N,n) with HasTangentPlane V x T (θ(x)) (Simon 8, Def. 1.1). Then for every S ∈ G(N,n): M has approximate tangent space S.plane at x with respect to θ (Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x S.plane, Simon Ch. 3, 1.7) if and only if S = T.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n), NullMeasurableSet M μHE[n] → (∀ y ∈ M, 0 < θ y) → (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) μHE[n]) → (∀ B : Set (Euclidean N), MeasurableSet B → V.weight B = ∫⁻ y in M ∩ B, ENNReal.ofReal (θ y) ∂μHE[n]) → HasTangentPlane V x T (θ x) → ∀ S : Grassmannian N n, Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x S.plane ↔ S = T
subproblems.natural_proof:
Import needed in Submission: Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.ConstancyTangent (Grassmannian.eq_of_plane_eq). Notation: H := μHE[n]; η_r := Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, so η_r(z) = r⁻¹•(z − x); G := Grassmannian N n.

1. What must be shown for T. HasWAT n M θ x T.plane consists of (i) finrank T.plane = n, which is Grassmannian.finrank_plane, and (ii) for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), ∫_{η_r(M)} g(y)·θ(x + r•y) dH(y) → θ(x)·∫_{T.plane} g dH as r ↓ 0. Fix g.

2. A test function on ℝ^N × G. Let f(z,S) := g(z). It is continuous, and it vanishes outside tsupport g × G. That set is compact, because tsupport g is compact and G is compact (Grassmannian.instCompactSpace). Hence f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ).

3. Apply the convergence clause of HasTangentPlane V x T (θ(x)) to f: ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x r) → θ(x)·∫ f d(planeVarifoldMeasure T) as r ↓ 0. On the plane side, planeVarifoldMeasure T = (H.restrict T.plane).map (y ↦ (y,T)). By integral_map (the map is continuous and f is continuous), ∫ f d(planeVarifoldMeasure T) = ∫_{T.plane} f(y,T) dH(y) = ∫_{T.plane} g dH.

4. Fix r > 0; we compute the rescaled side. By definition, rescaledMeasure V x r = ofReal(r⁻¹^n) • V.measure.map ψ_r with ψ_r(z) = (r⁻¹•(z.1 − x), z.2). By integral_smul_measure and ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (r⁻¹^n ≥ 0), and then integral_map (ψ_r continuous, f continuous):
 ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x r) = r⁻¹^n · ∫ g(r⁻¹•(z.1 − x)) dV.measure(z).
 Since V.weight = V.measure.map Prod.fst and y ↦ g(r⁻¹•(y − x)) is continuous, integral_map gives
 ∫ g(r⁻¹•(z.1 − x)) dV.measure(z) = ∫ g(r⁻¹•(y − x)) dV.weight(y).

5. Still with r > 0. Apply the sibling child integral_eq_weighted (Submission.allard_tc_tpr_integral_eq_weighted) to μ := V.weight, M and θ; its hypotheses are exactly ours. With the function z ↦ g(r⁻¹•(z − x)) it gives
 ∫ g(r⁻¹•(z − x)) dV.weight(z) = ∫_M g(r⁻¹•(z − x))·θ(z) dH(z).
 Apply the sibling child blowup_set_integral (Submission.allard_tc_tpr_blowup_setIntegral) with φ(y) := g(y)·θ(x + r•y):
 ∫_{η_r(M)} g(y)·θ(x + r•y) dH(y) = r⁻¹^n · ∫_M g(η_r z)·θ(x + r•η_r z) dH(z).
 Since η_r z = r⁻¹•(z − x) and x + r•(r⁻¹•(z − x)) = z (smul_smul, r·r⁻¹ = 1, one_smul, add_sub_cancel), the last integrand is g(r⁻¹•(z − x))·θ(z). Combining with step 4:
 ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x r) = ∫_{η_r(M)} g(y)·θ(x + r•y) dH(y) for every r > 0.

6. The interval (0,∞) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). So the two functions of r in step 5 are eventually equal along 𝓝[>] 0. By Tendsto.congr' and step 3, the weighted blow-up integrals ∫_{η_r(M)} g(y)·θ(x + r•y) dH(y) converge to θ(x)·∫_{T.plane} g dH. With step 1(i), HasWAT n M θ x T.plane holds.

7. The equivalence.
 (⇐) If S = T, this is step 6.
 (⇒) Suppose HasWAT n M θ x S.plane. HasTangentPlane V x T (θ x) includes 0 < θ(x), so θ(x) ≠ 0. The uniqueness theorem Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, applied to S.plane and T.plane (step 6), gives S.plane = T.plane. Points of G are determined by their planes (Grassmannian.eq_of_plane_eq), so S = T. ∎
proof_key_steps: Test Def. 1.1 with f(z,S) = g(z) ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) (G compact); the plane side gives θ(x)∫_{T.plane} g dH^n.
For r > 0: ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x r) = r^{-n} ∫ g(r⁻¹(z − x)) dμ_V(z) (integral_smul_measure, integral_map, μ_V = V.measure.map fst).
Sibling integral_eq_weighted: ∫ g(r⁻¹(z−x)) dμ_V = ∫_M g(r⁻¹(z−x))θ(z) dH^n.
Sibling blowup_set_integral with φ(y) = g(y)θ(x + r y): this equals r^n ∫_{η_r(M)} g(y)θ(x + r y) dH^n, so Tendsto.congr' gives HasWAT n M θ x T.plane.
Uniqueness: θ(x) > 0, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique and Grassmannian.eq_of_plane_eq give HasWAT S.plane ⟺ S = T.
